items.title: Conformal electrovacuum seed data
items.design_state: Defines smooth conformal electrovacuum seed data and its exact types, weights, units, and nonexistence scope.
items.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty oriented smooth three-manifold without boundary. items.title: Exact conformal electrovacuum constraint transformation
items.design_state: Derives the exact divergence, norm, trace, curvature, Hamiltonian, and retained momentum transformations from the stated seed and SI constraints.
items.statement: Use the smooth conformal seed data defined in this development on an oriented smooth three-manifold, and let $D$ and $\bar D$ be the Levi-Civita connections of $h=\psi^4\bar h$ and $\bar h$. Define $\Delta_{\bar h}\psi:=\bar h^{ij}\bar D_i\partial_j\psi$, with the Euclidean convention $\Delta=\sum_i\partial_i^2$ in Cartesian coordinates. Use the spatial curvature sign and scalar-curvature contraction fixed for induced data in the preceding Gauss-Codazzi convention. items.title: RN conformal data on a punctured exterior
items.design_state: Verifies the RN isotropic puncture data on its positive domain, including the nonextreme minimal sphere, both ends, and the exterior radial-coordinate match.
items.statement:
Let $m>0$ be a geometric mass length, let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a signed geometric electric-charge length, and define

$$r_*:=\max\left\{0,\frac{|q|-m}{2}\right\},\qquad \mathcal D_{m,q}:=(r_*,\infty),\qquad \psi(r):=\sqrt{\left(1+\frac{m}{2r}\right)^2-\frac{q^2}{4r^2}}\quad(r\in\mathcal D_{m,q}),$$

where the square root is positive. On $\Sigma=\mathcal D_{m,q}\times S^2$, use the Euclidean seed metric $\bar h=dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2}$, with $\gamma_{S^2}$ the unit round metric, and set

$$\bar E=q\,r^{-2}\partial_r,\qquad \bar B=0,\qquad \bar A=0,\qquad \tau=0,\qquad \Lambda=0.$$

With $h=\psi^4\bar h$, $K=0$, $E=\psi^{-6}\bar E$, and $B=0$, the exact transformed equations are

$$\bar D_i\bar E^i=0,\qquad \bar D_i\bar B^i=0,\qquad -8\Delta_{\bar h}\psi-2|\bar E|_{\bar h}^2\psi^{-3}=0,$$

and the separate momentum equation is $0=-2\psi^{-6}(\bar E\times_{\bar h}\bar B)_i$. They are satisfied by the displayed fields, so the corresponding SI-convention data satisfy the original constraints. The puncture $r=0$ is omitted from $\Sigma$, so the assertion concerns smooth equations on this domain and introduces no delta-function source there.

For $m>|q|$, $\mathcal D_{m,q}=(0,\infty)$. The centered coordinate sphere $S_r=\{r\}\times S^2$ has area $4\pi R_{\rm areal}(r)^2$, where

$$R_{\rm areal}(r):=r\psi(r)^2=r+m+\frac{m^2-q^2}{4r}.$$

On each $S_r$, the outward unit normal is $\nu:=\psi^{-2}\partial_r$. Define its mean-curvature scalar by $H:=\operatorname{div}_h\nu$; by convention here, $S_r$ is minimal exactly when $H(r)=0$. Its mean curvature vanishes exactly at $r_0=\frac12\sqrt{m^2-q^2}$, where $R_{\rm areal}(r_0)=m+\sqrt{m^2-q^2}$. Both ends are asymptotically Euclidean in the following explicit sense. In the Euclidean seed Cartesian coordinates $x^i=r n^i$ with $n\in S^2$, the $r\to\infty$ end has $h_{ij}=\left(1+2m/r+O(r^{-2})\right)\delta_{ij}$, $\partial_kh_{ij}=O(r^{-2})$, and $\partial_\ell\partial_kh_{ij}=O(r^{-3})$. For the inner end define inverted Cartesian coordinates $\tilde x^i:=(r_0^2/r^2)x^i$, whose radius is $\tilde r:=|\tilde x|=r_0^2/r$; the same metric and derivative falloffs hold as $r\downarrow0$ in these coordinates. On the branch $r>r_0$, put $R:=R_{\rm areal}(r)$. The comparator spatial metric is

$$h_{\rm RN}^{\rm spatial}:=f(R)^{-1}dR\otimes dR+R^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad f(R):=1-\frac{2m}{R}+\frac{q^2}{R^2},$$

with $R>m+\sqrt{m^2-q^2}$ and hence $f(R)>0$; the spatial metric $h$ agrees with this static Reissner–Nordström exterior metric under the displayed areal-radius coordinate. These statements make no global event-horizon or maximal-extension claim.

references.title: A. I. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009)
references.locator: Section III.B, equations (3.15)-(3.16), gives the single Reissner-Nordström isotropic conformal factor and radial electric field; the constraint verification here is direct.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012), author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1

title: Conformal constraint weights and charged time-symmetric data — Examples

items.title: Extremal cylindrical puncture end
items.design_state: Verifies the equal-mass/absolute-charge branch has an infinite-distance cylindrical puncture end and no centered minimal sphere.
items.statement:
Let $m=|q|>0$ in the one-hole Reissner–Nordström (RN) conformal-data family; this equality defines its extremal parameter case. Use the punctured spatial manifold $\Sigma=(0,\infty)\times S^2$. Then $\psi^2=1+m/r$, $h:=\psi^4(dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2})$, and the centered sphere is $S_r:=\{r\}\times S^2$, with areal radius $\rho(r):=r\psi^2=r+m$. On each $S_r$ use the outward unit normal $\nu:=\psi^{-2}\partial_r$ and define the mean-curvature scalar $H:=\operatorname{div}_h\nu$; a sphere is minimal exactly when $H=0$. With this convention, no centered coordinate sphere is minimal. The proper radial coordinate

$$s(r):=r+m\log(r/m)$$

has range $\mathbb R$ and gives

$$h=ds^2+(r(s)+m)^2\gamma_{S^2}.$$

As $r\downarrow0$, $s\to-\infty$ and $r(s)+m\to m$, so this end is asymptotic to the product cylinder $\mathbb R\times S^2$ with round-sphere radius $m$. The puncture is omitted; no point-source interpretation or global event-horizon claim is part of this example.

references.title: A. I. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009)
references.locator: Section III.B, equations (3.15)-(3.16), gives the one-hole RN seed; the end and proper-distance statements here are proved directly.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012), author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1
references.locator: Section 6.2.3, equations (6.22)-(6.24), supplies the isotropic spatial metric convention; the limiting cylinder is computed directly here.

items.title: Unscaled electric vectors fail the transformed Gauss law
items.design_state: Computes a smooth Euclidean counterexample showing the unscaled electric vector violates the transformed divergence constraint.
items.statement: The assignment $E=\bar E$ always preserves the source-free electric divergence constraint under $h=\psi^4\bar h$.

references.title: A. I. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009)
references.locator: Section III.A, equations (3.6)-(3.10), derives the divergence-preserving vector weight; this explicit counterexample tests the incorrect unscaled assignment.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012), author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1
